title: A local ring is henselian (idempotent lifting) iff simple roots of monic polynomials lift
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m,\kappa)$ be a local ring. The following are equivalent: (i) $R$ is henselian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], i.e. for every finite $R$-algebra $B$ every idempotent of $B/\mathfrak mB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$; (ii) for every monic polynomial $f\in R[T]$ and every $a_0\in\kappa$ with $\overline f(a_0)=0$ and $\overline{f'}(a_0)\neq0$ (where $\overline f\in\kappa[T]$ is the reduction of $f$) there exists $a\in R$ with $f(a)=0$ and $a\bmod\mathfrak m=a_0$.

source.place: algebra.tex Definition Tag 04GF (definition-henselian; Section Tag 04GE: (ii) is Stacks' definition of a henselian local ring) and Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), (1)<=>(10) (every finite R-algebra is a finite product of local rings); more-algebra.tex Definition Tag 09XE (definition-henselian-pair) with the remark following it (for a local ring, (R,m) is a henselian pair iff R is henselian) and Lemma Tag 09XI (lemma-characterize-henselian-pair), (1)<=>(3) (idempotents of B/IB lift uniquely for finite B)

proof.text: *Uniqueness of lifts holds for every local ring.* Let $B$ be a finite $R$-algebra and $e,e'\in B$ idempotents with $e\equiv e'\bmod\mathfrak mB$. Put $d=e-e'\in\mathfrak mB$. Expanding with $e^2=e$, $e'^2=e'$: $d^2=e-2ee'+e'$ and $d^3=d\cdot d^2=(e-2ee'+ee')-(ee'-2ee'+e')=e-e'=d$, so $d(1-d^2)=0$. Since $d^2\in\mathfrak mB$ and $\mathfrak mB$ lies in the Jacobson radical of $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical], $1-d^2$ is a unit of $B$; hence $d=0$, i.e. $e=e'$. So for every finite $R$-algebra $B$ the reduction map from idempotents of $B$ to idempotents of $B/\mathfrak mB$ is injective, and (i) amounts to its surjectivity for all finite $B$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 09XF (lemma-idempotents-determined-modulo-radical) and its use in the proof of Lemma Tag 09XI ((2)=>(4): IB lies in the Jacobson radical of B for B integral, so idempotents are determined modulo IB); 09XF is proved there by localizing at maximal ideals, here by the identity d^3=d

Let $S=R[T]/(f)$: it is a free $R$-module with basis $1,T,\dots,T^{n-1}$, hence a finite $R$-algebra, and $S/\mathfrak mS\cong\kappa[T]/(\overline f)$ [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free]. Let $ ar e\in S/\mathfrak mS$ be the idempotent corresponding to $(1,0)$, so that $ ar e(S/\mathfrak mS)\cong\kappa[T]/(T-a_0)\cong\kappa$ as quotients of $\kappa[T]$. By (i) [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] there is an idempotent $e\in S$ lifting $ ar e$. Then $S=eS	imes(1-e)S$, and $A=eS$ is a ring (unit $e$) and an $R$-algebra, a quotient of $S$ via $s\mapsto es$, and an $R$-module direct summand of the finite free $R$-module $S$; so $A$ is finitely generated and flat (a direct summand of a flat module is flat), hence free [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free]. Moreover $A/\mathfrak mA= ar e(S/\mathfrak mS)\cong\kappa$, so a basis of $A$ has exactly one element (its image is a $\kappa$-basis of $A/\mathfrak mA$): $A=Rb$ freely. Write $e=ub$ with $u\in R$; $e$ is the unit of $A$ and $A/\mathfrak mA
eq0$, so $e
otin\mathfrak mA$, i.e. $u
otin\mathfrak m$, and $u$ is a unit; hence $e$ is also a basis and the structure map $R	o A$, $r\mapsto re$, is an isomorphism of $R$-algebras. Let $a\in R$ be the image of $T$ under the $R$-algebra map $\varphi:R[T]	o S	o A\cong R$; then $\varphi$ is evaluation at $a$, and $f(a)=\varphi(f)=0$ because $f=0$ in $S$. Reducing modulo $\mathfrak m$, $\varphi$ followed by $R	o\kappa$ equals $R[T]	o S/\mathfrak mS	o ar e(S/\mathfrak mS)\cong\kappa[T]/(T-a_0)\cong\kappa$, which sends $T$ to $a_0$; hence $a mod\mathfrak m=a_0$. source.place: Lemma Tag 04GG (lemma-characterize-henselian), proof of 10=>1 (S=R[T]/(f), the factor with residue ring kappa[T]/(T-a_0) is finite free of rank 1, hence equal to R, and the image of T is the root), with the factor obtained from the lifted idempotent as in more-algebra.tex Lemma Tag 09XI, proof of (3)=>(1)

proof.text: *(ii)$\Rightarrow$ etale retractions (Stacks' condition (8)).* Assume (ii). Then for every ring map $R\to R'$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R'\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ etale and every prime $\mathfrak m'\subset R'$ over $\mathfrak m$ with $\kappa\to\kappa(\mathfrak m')$ an isomorphism there is a (unique) $R$-algebra map $\tau:R'\to R$ with $\tau^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m'$ [lem-weil-pbc-root-lifting-etale-retraction].

*Etale retractions $\Rightarrow$ finite algebras split (Stacks (8)$\Rightarrow$(10)).* By step 3 the hypothesis of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-retraction-finite-product-local] holds for $R$, so every finite $R$-algebra $B$ is isomorphic as an $R$-algebra to a finite product $B_1\times\cdots\times B_r$ of local rings.

*(ii)$\Rightarrow$(i): products of local rings lift idempotents.* Assume (ii) and let $B$ be a finite $R$-algebra; by step 4 we may take $B=B_1\times\cdots\times B_r$ with each $B_i$ local, with maximal ideal $\mathfrak n_i$. Each $B_i$ is a quotient of $B$ (projection), hence a finite $R$-algebra, so $\mathfrak mB_i\subset\mathfrak n_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-local-radical]; thus $\bar B_i=B_i/\mathfrak mB_i$ is a nonzero local ring. Since $\mathfrak mB=\prod_i\mathfrak mB_i$ (an element $\sum_k x_k(b_{k,i})_i$, $x_k\in\mathfrak m$, has components $\sum_kx_kb_{k,i}\in\mathfrak mB_i$, and conversely $(y_i)_i=\sum_i\epsilon_iy_i$ with $\epsilon_i$ the $i$-th unit vector), $B/\mathfrak mB\cong\prod_i\bar B_i$ componentwise. A local ring has no idempotents besides $0,1$ (if $\epsilon^2=\epsilon$, one of $\epsilon$, $1-\epsilon$ is a unit and $\epsilon(1-\epsilon)=0$). Idempotents of a product are computed componentwise, so every idempotent of $B/\mathfrak mB$ is $(\epsilon_i)_i$ with $\epsilon_i\in\{0,1\}\subset\bar B_i$; the element $(\epsilon_i)_i\in\prod_iB_i=B$ (same $0$s and $1$s) is an idempotent of $B$ reducing to it. With the uniqueness of step 1, every idempotent of $B/\mathfrak mB$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $B$: $R$ is henselian in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology]. Together with step 2 this proves (i)$\Leftrightarrow$(ii).

lean.statement: theorem idempotent_lifting_iff_monic_simple_root_lifting (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] : (∀ (B : Type (max u v)) [CommRing B] [Algebra R B] [Module.Finite R B], ∀ e₀ : B ⧸ (maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R B), IsIdempotentElem e₀ → ∃! e : B, IsIdempotentElem e ∧ Ideal.Quotient.mk ((maximalIdeal R).map (algebraMap R B)) e = e₀) ↔ (∀ f : Polynomial R, f.Monic → ∀ a₀ : ResidueField R, Polynomial.aeval a₀ f = 0 → Polynomial.aeval a₀ f.derivative ≠ 0 → ∃ a : R, f.IsRoot a ∧ residue R a = a₀)
lean.note: The idempotent condition is spelled out inline, as directed by the lean.note of def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology; the other side spells out the residue-field condition of HenselianLocalRing.TFAE. No private henselian predicate is introduced.
